paragraphs: Jordan needs new sneakers for the school running club. At a sports shop, the assistant asks what kind of shoes Jordan wants. Jordan replies, "I won't choose a pair {{mask_1}} it feels comfortable when I walk. I can try this model {{mask_2}} there is space for my toes."

The assistant explains that shoes should fit well, not just look good. "You shouldn't buy them {{mask_3}} your heel slips when you walk. You can compare another size {{mask_4}} you keep both shoes on while you test the fit." Jordan tries a different pair and walks slowly across the shop.

Jordan's friend Casey is shopping too. Casey likes a bright pair with thin soles. Jordan says, "You may enjoy that style {{mask_5}} it supports your feet well. You shouldn't use it for long runs {{mask_6}} the shop label says it is made for running." Casey checks the product information before deciding.

The assistant talks about caring for sneakers. "They will last longer {{mask_7}} you let them dry after a wet walk. Don't put them near a heater {{mask_8}} the care label says it is safe." Jordan asks about cleaning them. The assistant replies, "You can use a soft brush {{mask_9}} you follow the cleaning instructions."

Jordan finds a pair that feels comfortable, but wants to check the price. "I won't buy them {{mask_10}} they fit my budget," Jordan says. The assistant points out a discount on last season's colors. "You can get the lower price {{mask_11}} you choose one of these colors." Casey finds a similar offer on another shelf.

Before they leave, the friends compare their choices. Casey says, "I won't wear these for the running club {{mask_12}} they feel secure when I jog." Jordan agrees and checks that the shoes are the right size. "You can keep your receipt {{mask_13}} you may need to exchange them." The assistant reminds them to check the store's return policy.

On their first club practice, Jordan tests the new sneakers on the track. The coach says, "You can start with an easy run {{mask_14}} you feel comfortable. You should continue {{mask_15}} you feel comfortable." Casey asks if they should wear the new shoes every day. Jordan replies, "They should feel comfortable {{mask_16}} you wear them for longer practice."

After practice, both friends clean dust from their shoes. Casey says, "I can use this cloth {{mask_17}} it does not damage the material." Jordan checks the care label again. "We shouldn't store the sneakers in a closed bag {{mask_18}} they are completely dry." They leave the shoes in a ventilated place.

A week later, Jordan says the sneakers still feel good. Casey asks whether the shop will accept an exchange for a different color. Jordan answers, "They may exchange them {{mask_19}} you bring the receipt and follow the return policy." The friends decide that comfort matters most. They will keep the shoes {{mask_20}} they continue to fit well.
